FAQ

Short answers about ArchRay capabilities, data boundaries, hosts and updates.

What is ArchRay?

ArchRay is an AI-first architecture visualiser. Install it into a repository, type /archray in your AI assistant, and it reads real source to produce layered, interactive, offline 3D/2D single-file HTML.

Does it upload my source?

No. Analysis runs inside the AI assistant session you authorize, and artifacts stay in the local .archray directory; the HTML is self-contained. Only an explicit update contacts GitHub Releases to read the version and verify the archive.

Which AI hosts are supported?

Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, Pi and Codex. Claude/Cursor/Pi use /archray; Codex uses $archray or /skills. Install with --agent all or a comma-separated list.

How do I install and update?

Download the release or run the bootstrap install.sh in the target repository root. Then use ./.archray/archray update --check followed by update; v0.4 and older need a one-time bootstrap upgrade.

How is it different from a generic AI diagram?

ArchRay separates semantic facts from deterministic layout: the AI records source evidence and dependencies, while the layout engine computes coordinates and 3D/2D projections. It focuses on traceable paths, offline delivery, layers, health and replaceability instead of a one-off image.

Which repositories is it for?

It fits repositories where you need to understand real layers, cross-layer dependencies, technical debt or migration options, especially when the map should be shared offline. It is not runtime monitoring or an automatic scanner; description-only maps need extra review.

How does ArchRay differ from Mermaid, Structurizr, and Eraser?

Mermaid is great for quick Markdown flowcharts inside docs, but raw LLM-authored Mermaid collapses into crossed lines on multi-layer codebases; Structurizr requires maintaining hand-written C4 DSL and a local/cloud server; Eraser uploads diagram metadata to SaaS servers. ArchRay lets your AI coding agent extract verified source facts into .archray/graph.json, then deterministically computes an offline 3D/2D single-file HTML map via ELK.

Can it handle large monorepos with thousands of files without tangled edges?

Yes. Rather than dumping every file into one flat graph, ArchRay groups code into architectural modules. Benchmarked on calcom/cal.com (7,712 tracked files), it distilled 33 modules, 75 edges, and 7 layers with dense subpackages collapsed (+N) by default and a 196ms Node ELK layout—plus instant single-layer or comma-separated slice filtering like frontend,data.

Does Windows corrupt Chinese architecture labels into ??? question marks?

Starting in v0.6.0, ArchRay enforces UTF-8 without BOM during schema validation, rejects lone ? or U+FFFD encoding corruption, decodes GB18030 or UTF-16 files safely when reading, and instructs coding agents to use native UTF-8 file writes instead of Windows PowerShell ANSI redirection.

How do I share the output offline or embed it in architecture docs?

The output .archray/index.html bundles the entire viewer, typography fallbacks, and 167 vector brand icons—anyone can double-click it locally over file://. From the toolbar, you can also export an unclipped full-bounds PNG, generate an offline QR share poster, or export/import view.json camera states.

Privacy Policy & Collaboration

Your source code never leaves your machine. Reach out directly for partnerships, custom workflows, or feedback.

ArchRay Privacy & Data Security Policy

  • 1. 100% Local Execution · Zero Source Upload ArchRay CLI and single-file HTML views run entirely offline on your machine. No source code, file paths, secrets, or architecture graphs are ever uploaded to archray.dev or external servers.
  • 2. Host Coding-Agent Boundary Source analysis happens solely inside your own authorized AI coding session (Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, Pi, or Codex) under your chosen provider’s terms.
  • 3. Zero Telemetry, Zero Cookies, MIT Auditable Generated HTML views and CLI tools contain zero analytics beacons or tracking cookies; update checks perform read-only GitHub Release SHA-256 verification.
